title: Trump-Iran war: Costco nearly doubles motor oil price and imposes purchase caps
body: The retail price shock and purchase restrictions at major wholesale channels signal mounting stress across downstream refined petroleum products. Refinery realignments, prioritizing gasoline and diesel yields over base oil stocks, threaten to constrain lubricant availability across auto maintenance supply chains. Trump's war in key production zones continue to push crude input costs higher, squeezing consumer discretionary spending while creating persistent inflationary friction across retail supply networks. Escalating energy market pressures have reached retail store shelves as Costco caps motor oil purchases and nearly doubles prices on house-brand products.Summary: Costco has placed purchase restrictions on motor oil products across its retail platform. A two-pack of Kirkland Signature fully synthetic motor oil has risen to $57.99, up from roughly $30. Kirkland motor oil purchases are restricted to one transaction per member account every seven days, capped at two items per purchase. Sales of Mobil 1 motor oil are capped at five items per member account, priced at $43.99 for a six-pack. The retail price spikes highlight wider market consequences linked to international conflict and secondary energy supply constraints. Largest US retail club operator Costco Wholesale has raised prices significantly on motor oil products and introduced strict rationing across its sales channels.

title: South Korea Import Price Growth Eases
body: South Korea's import prices rose 15.6% year over year in August 2026, moderating from an 18.8% increase in July. The overall advance was driven primarily by raw materials, which surged 26.6%. Prices of intermediate goods climbed 16.6%, while capital goods and consumer goods saw more modest increases of 0.7% and 2.2%, respectively. By economic sector, prices of mining products jumped 28.8%, reflecting higher costs for coal, crude petroleum and natural gas (up 29.4%), as well as metallic and non-metallic mineral products (up 27.1%). Prices for manufactured goods rose 11.3%, led by a 44.5% surge in coal and petroleum products and a 21.5% gain in basic metal products. Meanwhile, prices for agricultural, forestry and marine products increased 6.7%. Within this category, marine product prices were up 11.7%, and agricultural product prices rose 10.9%. title: South Korea Export Price Growth Eases
body: South Korea's export prices rose 42.4% year over year in August 2026, slowing from a 48.9% increase in July. Among major categories, prices for manufactured goods climbed 42.4%, driven by a 113.2% surge in computers, electronic, and optical equipment. Prices were also higher for coal and petroleum products (65.9%), basic metal products (20.2%), and chemical products (14.0%). Prices for agricultural, forestry, and marine products increased 28.4% over the same period. On a monthly basis, however, the Export Price Index fell 3.7%. The Export Volume Index grew 25.9% year over year, while the Export Value Index jumped 75.8%. The Net Barter Terms of Trade Index also improved, rising 27.1%. title: South Korea's Export Price Growth Cools Sharply in August, Signaling Easing External Price Pressures
body: South Korea's Export Price Index growth eased notably in August 2026, pointing to a moderation in external price pressures for the trade-dependent economy. Year-over-year export prices rose 42.4% in August, down from a revised 49.1% annual increase recorded in July 2026. The data, updated on 14 September 2026, show that while export prices remain significantly higher than a year earlier, the pace of increase is slowing. The comparison is based on changes in prices for the reported month relative to the same month a year before, with the "previous" figure reflecting July's year-over-year change and the "actual" capturing August's performance versus August of the prior year. The deceleration in export price growth may indicate some easing of cost pressures for global buyers of South Korean goods, even as elevated price levels persist. Analysts and market participants will be watching whether the August slowdown marks the start of a broader trend toward more moderate export price inflation in the coming months. title: Crude Oi Nears $102 Amid Supply Disruptions
body: Crude oil hovered near $102 a barrel on Monday after briefly touching a four-month high of $105 earlier in the session. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Ukraine is prepared to halt strikes on Russian energy infrastructure if Moscow agrees to do the same. He stressed, however, that "Ukraine is not convinced that Russia is willing to abide by any agreement." Zelenskyy's conditional offer undercut US President Donald Trump's assertion that Russia and Ukraine had already agreed to suspend attacks on each other's energy facilities. At the same time, Saudi Arabia shut down a key pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz, tightening global supply conditions. Drones launched from Iraq damaged the kingdom's East–West pipeline on Thursday, prompting the Saudi government to close the route. A planned diplomatic meeting between Iran and Gulf Arab states to address tensions in the Strait of Hormuz was abruptly postponed after the pipeline attack. Over the weekend, the number of commodity vessels observed transiting the strait fell to single digits. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: Ibovespa Falls on Oil Rally and Political Uncertainty
body: The Ibovespa fell 0.9% on Monday, closing at 185,501, pressured by a rebound in oil prices and ongoing political uncertainty. Oil rose after Saudi Arabia shut down a key pipeline that bypasses the Strait of Hormuz. A diplomatic meeting in Oman between Iran and Gulf Arab states, scheduled for Monday to discuss the Hormuz situation, was abruptly postponed following the attack on the pipeline. Renewed energy-driven inflation concerns ahead of interest-rate decisions by both the BCB and the Fed weighed on credit-sensitive stocks. Major banks retreated, with Itaú down 0.9% and Bradesco down 1.4%. Utilities also closed lower, led by a 1.5% drop in Eneva. Political risk remained elevated amid the ongoing Supreme Court crisis, while new election polls confirmed a tight presidential race between President Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. Brazil's stock-market volatility index rose 5.24%. Vale sank 3.5% as iron ore prices in China ended the session lower. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com

title: TSX Closes Flat After CPI Data
body: The S&P/TSX Composite Index ended Monday's session virtually unchanged at 35,702 following the release of August CPI data. Headline inflation held steady at 3.0%, in line with market expectations. The ongoing conflict in the Middle East continued to support higher energy costs, with gasoline prices surging 22.8% year-on-year. The Bank of Canada's preferred core inflation measures—the median and trimmed-mean—were also stable, at 2.0% and 1.9%, respectively. These figures indicate that underlying price pressures remain contained, even as the BoC grows more concerned about inflation risks related to the war. Governor Macklem cautioned earlier this month that the longer the conflict endures, the greater the likelihood that elevated energy prices will filter through the broader economy. Investors largely anticipate a rate hike from the US Federal Reserve on Wednesday. Financial stocks mostly moved lower in response to rising yields. Weaker gold prices weighed on the materials sector, with Barrick and Wheaton Precious Metals each dropping 2.7%. Celestica sank 8.4%, mirroring a broad selloff in US semiconductor names. title: US Stocks Drop on Chipmaker Selloff
body: US equity indices ended lower on Monday, weighed down by a broad selloff in chipmakers. The S&P 500 slipped 0.5%, the Nasdaq 100 declined 0.8%, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 152 points. Sentiment toward AI-related names cooled after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for slowing the pace of AI development to mitigate risks from increasingly powerful models—an appeal publicly supported by OpenAI's Sam Altman and xAI's Elon Musk. The heightened focus on AI risks curbed speculative demand for chipmakers and AI infrastructure stocks. Nvidia fell 3.4%, Broadcom dropped 4.8%, Micron declined 5.2%, and Intel slid 5.6%. Among equipment and industrial names, Lam Research sank 8.3%, while GE Vernova slumped 8.6%. In fixed income, the 10-year Treasury yield briefly moved above 5% for the first time since 2023, as surging crude prices stoked fresh inflation worries ahead of Wednesday's Federal Reserve decision. Markets largely expect a 25-basis-point rate increase. The rejection of talks with GCC states extended the suspension of tanker flows from the region, further lifting energy prices. Additional losses in banking and manufacturing shares added pressure on the Dow. The material has been provided by InstaForex Company - www.instaforex.com
